questions.question: In which city was Yalta born and raised?
options: Nehardea
Pumbedita
Sura
Mechoza
questions.explanation: Nehardea, a flourishing Jewish center on the banks of the Euphrates, was destroyed in 259 in the revolt of Papa bar Netzer.

questions.question: True or false: Yalta was the wife of Rav Nachman.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: Rav Nachman was a young orphan, the son of Rav Yaakov, a scribe and judge in the court of Shmuel.

questions.question: What status did Rav Nachman acquire through his marriage to Yalta?
options: Head of the yeshiva of Sura
"Chatna de-vei nesiah," son-in-law of the house of the Exilarch
The Exilarch himself
A judge in the court of Rabbi Yochanan
questions.explanation: The status gave him great political and legal power and exceptional wealth.

questions.question: Which rule did Yalta formulate in her conversation with Rav Nachman (Chullin 109b)?
options: "Whoever forbids himself [things] shall be called holy"
"In a doubt concerning a rabbinic law, rule leniently"
"Everything the Merciful One has forbidden us, He has permitted us its equivalent"
"Everything follows custom"
questions.explanation: For everything that the Torah forbade, it permitted something similar to it in taste, in eating and in marital relations.

questions.question: True or false: According to Yalta, the Torah is meant to prevent a person from enjoying the pleasures of this world.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: In her view the Torah does not suppress pleasure but steers it toward the permitted. This is a response to ascetic approaches.

questions.question: What taste did Yalta ask to taste, and what did Rav Nachman instruct his cooks?
options: The taste of libation wine: to pour her cooked wine
The taste of a Gentile's bread: to bake her bread in his house
The taste of terumah: to bring her challah
The taste of meat with milk: to roast her an udder
questions.explanation: The udder contains meat and absorbed milk, and may be eaten when it is torn and roasted.

questions.question: On what did Ulla base his refusal to give Yalta from the cup of blessing?
options: "The fruit of a woman's womb is blessed from the fruit of a man's womb"
That a woman may not drink wine
That the cup had already been drunk
That Yalta did not hear the blessing
questions.explanation: So, according to him, Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Natan ruled: "And He will bless the fruit of your womb," and not "the fruit of her womb."

questions.question: True or false: When Ulla refused, Yalta smashed four hundred barrels of wine.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: She rose in anger ("bizihara") and went down to the wine cellar. According to the research, this was a demonstrative act and not a fit of rage.

questions.question: What did Yalta reply to Ulla, who sent her the message that "all the wine in the barrel is a cup of blessing"?
options: "There is no wisdom for a woman except at the spindle"
"From gathered words, and from rags, lice"
"Everything the Merciful One has forbidden us, He has permitted us its equivalent"
"You have spoken well"
questions.explanation: "From gathered words" (mimahaduri milei): his ruling is a collection of hearsay by a nomad, and not deep study.

questions.question: True or false: According to the Ben Ish Chai, the smashing of the barrels raises no halakhic difficulty.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: He asked how Yalta, a scholarly woman, transgressed "do not destroy" (bal tashchit) and the breaking of vessels in anger.

questions.question: Why did Yalta turn to another sage when Rabbah bar bar Chana declared impure the blood that she brought?
options: Because he was not authorized to rule
Because he ruled contrary to Shmuel
Every day he used to declare such a stain pure, and only on that day his eyes pained him
Because he made an error in counting the days
questions.explanation: Rav Yitzchak son of Rav Yehuda declared it pure. This is how the rule "a sage who has declared impure, his colleague may not declare pure" was reconciled.

questions.question: Who harassed Rav Amram Chasida, until Yalta saved him?
options: The soldiers of King Shapur
The students of Rav Yehuda
His neighbors in Nehardea
The servants of the house of the Exilarch, her family's house
questions.explanation: They laid him down on the snow and afterwards fed him fatty meat and neat wine.

questions.question: True or false: Yalta healed Rav Amram Chasida by seating him in hot water in a bathhouse.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: In this way the sweat was expelled from his body and he was healed: medical knowledge and moral courage in the face of the servants of her father's house.

questions.question: True or false: Rav Yehuda agreed to send greetings to Yalta, as Rav Nachman requested.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: He refused, in the name of Shmuel: "One does not greet a woman at all," not even through her husband.

questions.question: What advice did Yalta send to Rav Nachman in the discussion with Rav Yehuda?
options: "Release him from his dispute, so that he does not make you like other ignoramuses"
"Invite him to a meal and make peace with him"
"Send him to the Exilarch"
"Excommunicate him as he excommunicated"
questions.explanation: End the discussion quickly, so that he does not present you as a simple man. Rav Nachman accepted her advice immediately.

questions.question: Why did Rav Nachman permit Yalta to go out on a festival in a litter, according to the Gemara?
options: Because she was ill in her legs
"Yalta is different, for she is fearful"
Because the road was muddy
Because she was very old
questions.explanation: Another explanation among the commentators: the needs of the many, because the public needed her.

questions.question: What did Rabbi Yitzchak Isaac HaLevi and Rabbi Aharon Hyman claim about Yalta's ancestry?
options: That she was the daughter of Shmuel
That she was the daughter of Rav Yehuda
That she was the daughter of the serving Exilarch, and that Rabbah bar Avuha was Rav Nachman's teacher and matched them
That she was a convert from the royal house
questions.explanation: According to the accepted tradition she is the daughter of Rabbah bar Avuha, but he did not serve as Exilarch, and he is described at first as a pauper.

questions.question: What is the meaning of "and from rags, lice" (umisamartutei kalmei), according to the research?
options: A curse that Ulla be humiliated
That her wine is old and spoiled
That Ulla did not wash his hands
A parable against generalization: just as Ulla in his worn clothes is not filthy, so excellent women should not be restricted
questions.explanation: Lice multiply in worn clothes, but it is clear that this does not apply to a great man like Ulla.

questions.question: According to Rabbi Kook in "Ein Ayah," what did Yalta demonstrate by smashing the barrels?
options: Her independent authority, and that excellent women have a principal place in leadership
A momentary anger from which nothing is to be learned
Contempt for the wealth of her father's house
A protest against drinking wine
questions.explanation: As a leader who was entrusted with the education of girls, she saw in Ulla's words a threat to her educational and public authority.

questions.question: What precedent arises from the permission "Yalta is different, for she is fearful," according to the research?
options: Women are exempt from observing the festival
Psychological distress and anxiety may justify leniency in laws of the public sphere
It is permitted to carry any person in the public domain
The custom of the house of the Exilarch overrides halakha
questions.explanation: Rav Nachman defined her fear of falling and of the crush of the crowd as a real need.
